title: Asa di Var close
hook: wonder, awe, sweetness, the thread of compassion

segments.voice: Yesterday, amrit vela, the ambrosial hours when the Asa di Var is sung. Today we close it: four weeks of the dawn ballad, gathered like a pauri.

When the dawn singing ends, the sangat doesn't scatter right away. People stand for Ardas. Karah prashad, the warm sweet offering, is passed hand to hand. Someone folds the white sheets. Outside, the sun is up and the streets are filling with buses and school uniforms. People walk out carrying almost nothing: no notes, no book. Maybe one line, still humming in the back of the head. That's one way the var travels: as lines people carry out the door.
screen: `ARDAS, AND KARAH PRASHAD.` → `THE SUN FULLY UP.` → `ONE LINE CARRIED OUT THE DOOR.`

segments.voice: Let's walk the staircase once, from the top. An old ballad of heroes, given new words and sung to a king's tune. A sacrifice to the Guru a hundred times a day, the Guru who made angels out of men. A hundred moons, and still dark without the Guru. The One who made Himself and watches with delight. Then four steps of seeing: vismaad, wonder at every sound and color; kudrat, power in seeing, eating, loving; bhau, the wind and rivers moving in awe; and nirbhau, nirankar, only the Formless without fear. Then the people: the contented ones who served. Haumai, ego as a chronic illness with its medicine inside it. Cartloads of books, and only one thing counted. Koorh, the false king and everything that passes. Sach, truth known only when the heart is true. Then the turnings: pain the medicine, pleasure the disease. Mitthat neevee, sweetness and humility, the heavy side of the scale. The silk-cotton tree, tall and useless. The sacrifice to the Guru who put wisdom on the eyes. Then the thread: compassion the cotton, contentment the thread, restraint the knot, truth the twist; a thread that won't break, burn, stain or be lost. Sootak moved inside: greed, lies, coveting, gossip. Fikka words that make a fikka life. The servant who argues. And the shape itself: pauris as steps, Guru Angad's second voice, the whole thing sung as the sky turns gold. If one thread runs through it all, it might be the one in the carry. The var keeps starting with wonder. Before it corrects anyone, it makes them look. Wonder first, then the work.
screen: `THE BALLAD, THE GURU, THE MOONS.` · `WONDER, POWER, AWE, THE FEARLESS.` · `EGO, KOORH, TRUTH, SWEETNESS.` · `THE THREAD, THE SERVANT, THE DAWN.` · then, large: `WONDER AT DAWN.`

segments.voice: Let the block pass through your mind once more, bhau, the simmal, the scale, the thread, dal without salt, the arguing servant, and wait for the one that keeps coming back. Say its picture to yourself in one sentence, then breathe with it, the way the sangat carries a line out the door. If you pray, you can say Waheguru.
Vismaad, wonder: twenty-four pauris and their saloks, sung at dawn, hold vismaad, awe, truth, sweetness, and the thread of compassion.
Your line: wonder at dawn. One line, carried out the door, is plenty. Four weeks of the dawn ballad, complete.

howItsDone: Sikhs hear the Asa di Var sung in gurdwaras each morning, followed by Ardas and karah prashad, and many carry a favorite salok from it through the day.

chat.says: You spent weeks on the Asa di Var. What's one thread through the whole thing?
options: It keeps starting in wonder: before it corrects anyone, it makes them look.
It's mostly a list of rules: what to eat, what to wear, and when to bathe.
It's mainly a record of the Gurus' battles, since a var is a ballad of heroes.
chat.meaning: The var keeps opening with vismaad, wonder at every sound and color; only after making us look does it turn to ego, truth and service.
